notes: LUM-1333 baseline — the *pre-fix* binary (`origin/feature/pi.rs` = 3e7af2761, built from the same tree) driven through the same real PTY with the same gestures as lum1333-autocomplete-pointer.json.

This scenario asserts the DEFECT, so it passes on the binary without the pointer routing: the press on a candidate row, the release that should accept it and the wheel notch inside the list all leave the dropdown exactly as it was, because none of them belonged to any layer — the press started a chat-log selection and the wheel went to the transcript viewport.
The fix turns every one of those assertions into the opposite (see lum1333-autocomplete-pointer.json, 20/20 PASS), which is what makes the pair an A/B rather than two unrelated screenshots.
caption: LUM-1333 baseline — the same gestures as the fixed run, on the pre-fix binary, and the same real PTY. Panel 1: `/` opens the menu (this much worked: the dropdown was painted before this round). Panel 2: the press on row 14 does nothing to the list — no '❯' on `new`, the window indicator stays at '(1/21)'. Panel 3: the release completes nothing: the composer still holds the bare `/` and the list is still up. Panel 4: the draft is cleared and `/` reopens the menu. Panel 5: the wheel notch over row 15 does not move the highlight — it was routed to the chat log, which has nothing to scroll here. Panel 6/7: same. Everything the fixed run does with the pointer is missing here, and nothing else changed.
